P1.evidence: P1a not applicable — no setter, and the prospect confirms he received nothing but the calendar invite. P1b partial, a three-part frame where the script asks four: "walk me through what's been going on with you. What are you trying to get to? And how can we actually help you? And if you can, I can guide you through." That covers where you are, where you want to go and how we help, but never what is in the way or what he needs. P1c miss — no agreement was sought and no "does that work?" was asked. P1d hit — "how can we actually help you?" is the open question and it produced a long, unprompted and genuinely useful answer.

P2.evidence: The baseline is unusually complete on the record and almost none of it was asked for. P2a miss — age 43, height 5'5" and weight 80 kg from a peak of 100 kg were all volunteered inside the opening monologue; the rep asked for none of them. P2b partial — remote work and being hunched over a device 80 percent of the day were volunteered, and the rep engaged with the consequence but never asked the question. P2c miss — health conditions, own or hereditary, never asked. P2d hit and correctly timed: "Do you have any injuries or any things that limits your movements?" followed by "So it's not popping up right now?", which is what surfaced both the ankle surgeries and the shoulder impingement. P2e and P2f partial — the training week and two years of results came out because the opener invited them, not because they were asked for. P2g is the strongest check on the call: "brief me in about the nutrition part too. Like, what does it look like right now?", then a push for specifics, then "in terms of, like, what do you eat for fun?" P2h miss and it matters — sleep was never asked, and the prospect volunteered at 00:47:55 that it had been "horrible over the last couple of weeks" with a newborn and was already costing him gym sessions. That arrived 47 minutes in, unprompted, and was acknowledged but not explored. P2i miss.

P3.evidence: The best-executed goals phase in the batch alongside the Yash call. P3a hit and cleanly framed: "If you'd have to name it like in your own words, like the biggest goal that you want to achieve right now, what is it?" P3c hit — the rep asked about returning to squash and badminton. P3f hit: "How about other kids? How old are they and are you playing with them too?" produced the four children including the newborn. P3g hit and driven hard — "you're 43 so you have to show up for them, you have to be active for them, like still for at least 20 years" plus the granddad-on-the-couch image. P3h is the standout and is close to script: "would it be, correct me if I'm totally off, but for me it sounds, it's not about 20% body fat below. It's about showing your son... make him an example that it's possible and he's going to be looking up to you." Answered "A hundred percent." P3d and P3e partial — the deeper-driver bridge was implied rather than asked, and the what-becomes-possible question was asked in a leading form that supplied its own answers ("Lower the body fat, being active with kids... Looking good").

P4.evidence: Diagnostically unrun but strategically effective. P4a through P4d are partial across the board because two years of self-directed work, the YouTube diet, the gym split and the self-designed kettlebell circuit were all volunteered rather than asked for; the closest the rep came was "how long have you been actually doing all of that?" P4e is a genuine hit and the best moment of the phase: the rep named the pattern — "that's actually the common trap that people fall into, that you have everything on YouTube right now, and you download and save, like, dozens of videos, but it's very difficult to actually put it together and follow through" — and the prospect named his own gap in response: "there's enough information out there in the web that you can probably, if you're disciplined enough, do it yourself. But I think it's the structure, it's the accountability... that was the reason I reached out." P4f partial: the rep made the argument rather than asking it, via a good consultant analogy — "in business, you can also find things on YouTube, but it's about the speed and dialing that in... you just shortcut the whole process" — aimed at a business owner, which is why it worked.

P5.evidence: Effectively absent. The only trace of a consequence frame is a passing image at 00:23:12 — "you don't want to be that the granddad that sits on the couch and like hand me the remote because I can't get to it" — delivered conversationally and agreed with in passing. That is worth a partial on P5a and nothing more. The two-year question was never asked, no settle test was run, no "why not", and no line in the sand. This is the fifth sales call in this batch and the fourth where P5 scores miss or partial; it is now clearly the rep's structural weakness rather than a one-off. The cost is visible in the same place every time: when the spouse and cash-flow objections arrived at 00:50, there was no established cost of waiting to weigh them against, so the entire response had to be payment mechanics and a busy-season reframe.

P6.evidence: P6b hit: "If we can figure out all the details. Are you going to be fully committed to showing up and doing the work to become a version of Siddiq?" answered "yeah, I'm fully committed, you know, I can do this quite comfortably... eager to get going." P6a partial — the belief question was asked about the training approach only ("This approach would actually work for you?" / "Yeah, it would. Of course, yeah."), never about getting there with the right structure and the right person in his corner. P6c partial and it is the same conditional-yes pattern as the other calls in this batch: the commitment was explicitly gated on "if we can figure out all the details", the details were the money, and the money had not been examined. The spouse consult surfaced within 90 seconds of the price. There was no Phase 5 to return to.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and deferred to a spouse conversation; no payment, agreement or onboarding step was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger at 00:50:36 — "let me just confirm with the missus." Three moves ran and two of them well. He established the prospect's own belief first, though as an assertion rather than the scripted money-aside question: "I understand that you're positive about it, that you can get to your goals with Trevor." He asked the obstacles question close to script: "when you talk to her today, like, do you feel that there might be any potential obstacles?" And he pre-framed the spouse's reaction usefully — "the missus, what hears is, okay, so my husband wants to get a fitness program for 6K... what's usually the answer. Like, are you crazy?" Three moves did not run and they were the decisive ones. He never asked whether there is any reason she would not want him stronger and less in pain. He never asked whether this genuinely needs her input or is permission to bet on himself, and he never used the this-is-not-a-joint-decision-like-buying-a-house line — despite the prospect handing him the opening by saying "it's a commitment for everyone... It does impact their life and lifestyle as well." And no deposit-with-refund fallback was offered, which is the scripted move for exactly this position and would have converted a soft deferral into a held deal. Worse, when the prospect raised the real obstacle — that his wife had just given birth and would reasonably ask "what about me?" — the rep amplified it rather than solving it: "She might be opposed to that, actually. I know you're pretty good about it, but her perspective is going to be totally different." That is the one thing the play exists to prevent.

The best-run play in the batch, then abandoned halfway. Trigger on timing across travel in July and September and the son's cricket tour. The rep ran the busy-season move directly — "with the timing aspect, like look, are there going to be any other, you know, busy season?" — and the prospect answered it for him: "things never slow down. It's busy all the time." He followed with "It doesn't matter whether you're going to start now or after summer" and got "Agreed, agreed. Agreed." That is the move landing exactly as designed. He then let it go. The prospect immediately reframed the objection from schedule to cash-flow timing ("So it's a timing of expenses, right?") and the rep did not re-run the play against the new frame, did not use "the longer you wait the harder this gets", did not use "the only thing you can control is right now", and did not ask what specifically was coming up that prevented him from getting started. He pivoted to third-party financing instead, which the prospect declined on principle.

Isolation was run and run well: "apart from the finances everything good?" answered "yeah everything doesn't make sense" — i.e. no other blocker. Two structures were then put on the table concretely, which is more than happened on any other non-closing call in this batch: $1,200 a month, and the recommended interest-free $3,000 plus $3,000 split. He also probed third-party financing. What did not run is the entire financial picture — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no card count, no available credit, no investments — and the SHOULD I versus HOW reframe was never used. The prospect did most of the work himself, volunteering that affordability was not the issue and liquidity timing was, which is precisely the information the picture questions are designed to surface and act on. Nothing was then built around it. Marked partial rather than hit chiefly because of the execution error captured in the flags file: the monthly figure was stated once as $1,200 and left uncorrected when the prospect twice repeated it back as $1,000.

No deliberation objection in substance. The deferral was to a specific person for a specific reason, not a request for thinking time — and the prospect was clear on his own position: "it's a no-brainer for me."
No fear or doubt about the method. He is already training with kettlebells at 20 kg and rates Trevor above every other creator he follows.

Clinical fit, in a milder but still unaddressed form. The prospect disclosed a right shoulder impingement injected with steroid roughly a month earlier, after physiotherapy failed, with his treating doctor flagging that failure would indicate "some bigger problem we need to go fix properly". The rep half-noticed the risk — "the weights that you said, they seem pretty high already" — and resolved it entirely inside the product: "definitely, Trevor will check your form." There is no scripted path for asking whether a clinician has cleared loaded overhead work, which is the same script gap logged from the Tyron Giuliani call, and it means a recently injected shoulder was routed to a form check. See the flags file.

notes: Strong front half, one avoidable error at the back. P3 was excellent — the reflect-back at 00:22:13 landed the real why on the first attempt — and P4e worked because the rep built the YouTube-trap frame and let the prospect name his own gap, which is exactly how that check is supposed to run. Three coaching points. First, P5 again: four of five sales calls in this batch have no consequence frame, and every one of them arrives at the objection with nothing to weigh it against. Second, on OB he ran the diagnostic moves and skipped the resolving ones — the deposit-with-refund fallback would have held this deal, and instead he agreed with the prospect that the wife might object. Third and most important, the monthly figure was quoted at $1,200 and the prospect twice restated it as $1,000 without correction, then left to present that number to his wife; correct the number before the follow-up call.
